Real GDP expanded by 7.7% in FY 2025-26, compared to 7.1% in the previous year, reflecting broad-based economic expansion despite an uncertain global environment.2 Depreciation pressure on the Rupee intensified during the second half of the year, driven by foreign portfolio outflows and a surge in crude oil prices.

While inflationary pressures persisted, primarily due to volatility in food prices, labour market conditions remained stable, with the Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) recorded at 59.3% in 2025.3 The power and energy sector continued to benefit from rising economic activity, increasing industrial demand and ongoing infrastructure development.
